ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, and point R is on the outside right side of the circle. Starting from R there are two secants: one horizontal secant passes through Q and P in order, where Q is near the right-side intersection point of the circle, P is near the left-side intersection point of the circle, and the figure marks PQ=12, QR=2; another slanted secant goes downward from R through the circle, passing through S and T in order, and the figure marks TS=3. Reasoning: From external point R, use the secant-secant theorem: the external segment multiplied by the whole secant is equal. The whole segment of the horizontal secant is RP=RQ+QP=2+12=14. Let RS=x, then the whole segment of the slanted secant is RT=RS+ST=x+3. Therefore RQ·RP=RS·RT, that is 2·14=x(x+3). Solving gives x^2+3x-28=0, factoring as (x-4)(x+7)=0. Length takes the positive value, so x=4, that is RS=4.

raw_record.question_text: Find $R S$ if $P Q=12, Q R=2,$ and $T S=3$.

method.method_draft: Use the secant-secant power theorem from the external point R. From the image, R is outside the circle and two secants pass through it: the horizontal secant goes R-Q-P with Q and P on the circle, and the slanted secant goes R-S-T with S and T on the circle. From the text, read PQ=12, QR=2, and TS=3. Compute the whole horizontal secant length RP=RQ+QP=2+12=14. Let RS=x, so the whole slanted secant RT=RS+ST=x+3. Apply RQ·RP=RS·RT: 2·14=x(x+3). Solve x^2+3x-28=0, giving x=4 as the positive length.

method.method_draft: Model the figure by assigning directed distances from R along each secant. From the image, the horizontal ray from R enters the circle at Q and exits at P, while the slanted ray from R enters at S and exits at T. From the text, the horizontal intersections are at distances RQ=2 and RP=2+12=14 from R. Therefore the circle cuts that line at parameters 2 and 14, so the product of the two directed intersection distances from R, i.e. the power magnitude along any secant, is 2·14=28. On the slanted secant, let the first intersection distance RS=x; since ST=3, the second intersection distance RT=x+3. The same product must hold for this line through R, so x(x+3)=28. Solving gives x=4, so RS=4.
